region.subtitle: The Last Refuge
story.origin: The captain tells of Sarpadia, a distant continent on Dominaria. Refugees carried its traditions to Shandalar before the Great Barrier. Their descendants call this island the Last Refuge; it is not the lost Sarpadia.
story.voyage: This ship crosses only Shandalar's sea. Help five communities resist the Ebon Crown, then challenge its lord. Passage home is always free.
story.danger: This is a dangerous land for experienced adventurers. Its roaming creatures are strong; the Crown's commanders have 26–30 life and its lord has 36. Build your deck and life on the mainland first if needed. Their strength does not follow yours.
story.gate: The final challenge needs all five pledges and at least half of your main deck's nonland cards from Fallen Empires. Lands and sideboard do not count. Community rewards can help build one or two colors.
story.vault: The first travelers hid their keepsakes in these vaults. No passage to Dominaria remains here. Explore for treasure and clues; this dungeon grants no pledge and is not required to challenge the Ebon Crown.
voyage.free: Refuge Harbor always offers a free voyage home. Petitions wait; mainland deadlines pause while you are away.
port.free.welcome: The captain welcomes the liberator of the Last Refuge. The communities are free.
port.free.return: Sail back to explore, trade or collect waiting rewards. Both voyages remain free.
port.island.ready: The ship is ready to take you home. Your work here will wait for your return.
castle.free.subtitle: The Last Refuge — Liberated
castle.free.broken: The Ebon Crown is broken. The communities govern themselves; the castle no longer commands their roads.
castle.intro: Beyond these gates rules the Lord of the Ebon Crown. Win the five communities' pledges and bring their spells to answer his challenge.
castle.count: Pledges: {pledges} of {quests_total}. Your main deck: {count} of {total} nonland cards are from Fallen Empires.
castle.required: Required: at least {required} Fallen Empires nonlands (at least {percent}%). All lands are excluded.
castle.carry: The communities ask you to carry their spells into this final challenge. No ante is staked; a loss or draw lets you try again.
quest.bread.title: The Bread Road
quest.bread.petition: Leitbur's Rest remembers Icatia's soldiers and its divisive zealots. Some keepers would feed only the faithful. Carry their grain warrant to Refuge Harbor for everyone, then return to defeat the Crown's tithe-collector.
quest.bread.epilogue: The grain wagons roll again. Leitbur's Rest pledges its aid, and its keepers agree that neither the Crown nor a zealot may decide who deserves bread.
quest.bread.guide: Bread Road: carry the grain warrant to {target}. The community provides the cargo.
quest.harbor.title: A Harbor for Both Peoples
quest.harbor.petition: Vodalian fishers and homarids have made a new harbor pact, despite their ancestors' wars. The Crown's captain commands sea magic to blockade them. Neither people trusts the other's charts. Survey the disputed channel first, then return to defeat the captain and reopen it to both.
quest.harbor.epilogue: The blockade is broken. Vodalian fishers and homarids mark shared channels through the harbor. Their pledge begins with safe passage for both peoples.
quest.harbor.guide: Harbor pact: survey the shared channel at {target}, then return to {town}.
quest.harbor.line: The fishers disagree about whose boats may use the channel. Record a shared route before asking either people to fight for the pact.
quest.masters.title: No More Masters
quest.masters.petition: Free thrulls live here beside people who rejected the Ebon Hand. The Crown's overseer would drag them back into breeding pits. Defeat him and defend their freedom.
quest.masters.epilogue: The overseer's bonds are broken. Free thrulls and those who rejected the Ebon Hand stand together: no life made by magic belongs to its maker.
quest.mountain.title: The Mountain Road
quest.mountain.petition: Dwarven smiths and goblin traders refuse to repeat their ancestors' wars. They share a mountain pass, but the Crown's raiders demand tribute. Both accuse the other of paying the raider. Seek him where the road's travelers shelter and break the tribute barrier there.
quest.mountain.epilogue: The tribute barriers come down. Dwarven smiths and goblin traders reopen their common road. Their pledge protects travelers, whatever their ancestry.
quest.mountain.guide: Mountain Road: confront the tribute-raider at {target}.
quest.mountain.line: Goblin carriers and dwarven smiths blame each other for the tolls. The Crown's raider collects from both. Hear their case before the duel.
quest.grow.title: Room to Grow
quest.grow.petition: Havenwood's elves and thallids tend an uneasy border. The Crown's sporekeeper spreads unchecked growth to drive them apart. Defeat the sporekeeper and protect the grove's balance.
quest.grow.epilogue: The sporekeeper retreats. Havenwood's elves and thallids can tend their border again, giving both woodland and fungus room to live. They offer you their pledge.
quest.reward_line: Reward, once: choose six Fallen Empires cards in one color, 40 gold, 8 food and a pledge.
quest.retry_line: No ante, deadline or deck-percentage requirement. A loss or draw lets you retry. Enemy life: {life}.
quest.secure: Your pledge is secure. Unclaimed rewards remain here or at the castle.
town.petition: The Last Refuge — {title}. Hear the community's petition here.
rewards.title: The Communities' Spells
rewards.intro: Choose six Fallen Empires cards in one color for each earned pledge. Any community can teach any color; repeat a color to strengthen one deck. Cards that do not fit your bag are kept safely.
rewards.rules: Copy limits and bans apply. If a color has too few eligible cards, choose another or return later; your reward stays owed.
rewards.pending_line: {count} reward cards are waiting at a community or the castle; make room in your bag to collect them.
rewards.collected: Collected {count} cards. {left} remain safely held for you.
deck.no_pack: Enable Pack 2: Fallen Empires in Options to begin this battle.
deck.empty: Choose a deck in a town's deck builder before beginning this battle.
deck.unknown: Your deck contains unavailable cards. Enable their packs or edit the deck in town.
deck.line: Last Refuge: FE nonlands {count}/{total} · need {required} · {pledges}/{quests_total} pledges
duel.leave_question: Return to the main menu? This unfinished battle is not saved. Your adventure resumes before the challenge.
duel.over: The battle is over. You may prepare and try again; no cards were staked.
duel.won_reward: You receive 40 gold and 8 food. Choose six cards in a color of your choice; you may collect them later.
duel.won_again: Its reward has already been collected or held for you.
duel.lost_log: Lost to {foe} on the Last Refuge.
duel.title: The Last Refuge
finale.freed: The Ebon Crown falls. The island is free! The five communities raise their banners, and the castle flies their gold pennant. Your main quest continues.
finale.already: The island is already free. Its communities welcome you.
finale.unmet: The battle is won, but the island's challenge still requires all five pledges and a qualifying deck.
status.ship: The ship at Refuge Harbor always offers a free voyage home.
task.finale.title: Liberate the Last Refuge
task.finale.text: {pledges}/{quests_total} pledges. The final deck needs at least {percent}% Fallen Empires nonlands.
task.rewards.title: Collect pledge rewards
task.rewards.text: Choose or collect your earned cards at a community or the castle.
task.rewards.done: All currently earned pledge rewards have been collected.
talk.news.free: The Ebon Crown has fallen. The communities keep their own councils. Refuge Harbor still offers free passage.
talk.news.bound: The Ebon Crown rules from the island's central castle. You hold {pledges} of {quests_total} pledges. Seek {target}. The five petitions have no time limit; ordinary town errands keep their own deadlines.
talk.applause.free:
The wise man says:
“The people thank you for freeing the Last Refuge.
talk.applause.bound:
The wise man says:
“The people welcome your help against the Ebon Crown.
talk.tribute.known: Your victories are known on this island.
talk.tribute.offer: The creature offers tribute. Will you...
talk.roam.free: The Ebon Crown is broken, but danger remains on the island.
talk.roam.bound: A roaming challenger bars your way on the Last Refuge.
tale.sarpadia.title: Memories of Sarpadia
tale.sarpadia: Our ancestors named Icatia, Vodalia, the Ebon Hand, the dwarven holds and Havenwood. Their histories tell of peoples divided against their neighbors and themselves. We keep those stories here so that a refuge need not become another fallen empire.
tale.crossing.title: The First Crossing
tale.crossing: The oldest account tells of a passage to Shandalar, before its Great Barrier. It names neither a surviving gateway nor a way to reopen it. The Vaults hold the travelers' keepsakes; the ship at our harbor sails only between this island and the mainland.
tale.bread.title: Bread and Belief
tale.bread: The Icatian traditions carried both protectors and zealots. Leitbur's Rest remembers the danger of letting fear decide who may share a harvest. Its people ask for an open road, not a new ruler.
tale.coast.title: A Shared Coast
tale.coast: Vodalian and homarid stories remember old wars. Here their descendants must live with the same tides. The harbor pact is new, fragile, and theirs to make; it does not change what happened in Sarpadia.
tale.freehold.title: The Freehold
tale.freehold: The Order of the Ebon Hand made thrulls to serve it. The free thrulls of this island reject that inheritance, alongside people who turned away from the Order. The Crown would restore the old bondage in the name of tradition.
tale.mountain.title: The Mountain Road
tale.mountain: The dwarves' tales remember wars with orcs and goblins. The traders of this island have chosen another bargain: shared work and passage through the mountains. The Crown profits when they distrust one another.
tale.forests.title: Room for Two Forests
tale.forests: Havenwood's stories warn of elves losing control of the thallids they cultivated. Here the border is tended with care. The Crown's sporekeeper spreads unchecked growth to break that peace, then offers the lord's protection at a price.
